proposal.description_long: The Philadelphia Inquirer reported on flight records obtained by McClatchy that showed two airport overlaps between aircraft associated with Dmitry Rybolovlev and Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign. On October 30, Rybolovlev’s plane landed in Las Vegas on the day Trump campaigned there; the report said the jet spent about an hour and 20 minutes on the ground and taxied to a private hangar used by casino owner Sheldon Adelson. On November 3, Rybolovlev’s aircraft arrived at Charlotte Douglas International Airport less than an hour after Trump’s campaign plane, while Trump appeared at a rally in nearby Concord. Rybolovlev’s representative said the trip was for business and that he had no contact with Trump or his advisers. The reported records document aircraft movements and the representative’s denial. They do not establish that either man was aboard at the same time, that the two men met or communicated, or that the travel was coordinated. The original wording “cross paths” overstates what the evidence establishes; this draft keeps the claim at aircraft proximity.
proposal.description_medium: A Philadelphia Inquirer report citing McClatchy flight records said Dmitry Rybolovlev’s aircraft landed in Las Vegas on October 30, 2016, when Trump held a rally there, and in Charlotte on November 3, near another campaign stop. The plane reached Charlotte less than an hour after Trump’s campaign aircraft. Rybolovlev’s representative denied contact. These movements do not prove the men met.
proposal.description_short: Flight-record reporting placed Rybolovlev’s jet near two Trump campaign stops in 2016; it does not establish that the men met or traveled together.
proposal.title: Reports Place Rybolovlev’s Jet Near Two 2016 Trump Campaign Stops
